title: Aztec Triple Alliance
capsule: The Ēxcān Tlahtōlōyān (Triple Alliance) was formed in 1428–1430 among the Nahua city-states of Tenochtitlan, Texcoco, and Tlacopan to overthrow Tepanec dominance; under the warrior-king Itzcoatl and his adviser Tlacaelel, it rapidly expanded into the dominant power of Mesoamerica. At its height under Ahuitzotl (r. 1486–1502) the Alliance exacted tribute from over 370 subject towns stretching from the Gulf Coast to the Pacific and from the Valley of Mexico south into Oaxaca and the Gulf lowlands, supporting a capital at Tenochtitlan estimated at 200,000–300,000 inhabitants. Hernán Cortés landed in 1519 and, exploiting subject-people resentments and epidemic disease, orchestrated the Alliance's defeat; Tenochtitlan fell on 13 August 1521 and the last tlatoani Cuauhtémoc was captured, ending independent Mexica rule.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The tribute lists (Codex Mendoza, Matrícula de Tributos) document the Alliance's subject towns with considerable precision; translating those lists into territorial boundaries involves scholarly inference, so peripheral regions are less certain than the core.
